where Kṛṣṇa becomes the eternal lord of the forest of Vṛndā; / Kṛṣṇa attained the status of Govinda—what need is there of other lengthy speeches?
The third petal is described as the best, the highest of the high among all. / The fourth petal is described as the place of most wondrous aesthetic joy.
The delightful grove Nandīśvara, where the abode of Nanda is remembered; / the glorification of the pericarp-petal is called the fifth petal.
The presiding deity here is the cowherd, devoted to the protection of the cattle. / The sixth petal that is described is remembered as the grove Nandavana.
The seventh is the Bakula forest, declared to be a delightful petal. / The eighth there is the Tāla forest; there the slaying of Dhenuka is remembered.
The ninth is the Kumuda forest, proclaimed to be a charming petal. / And the Kāmya forest is the tenth, the primary cause of everything.
The dressing of Brahmā and the display of the disguise of Viṣṇu are there; / it is called the primary petal, the place of the aesthetic joy of Kṛṣṇa's play.
The eleventh petal is proclaimed as the cause of grace to devotees: / the construction of the bridge, a place composed of various forests.
Bhāṇḍīra is the twelfth petal, a charming and captivating forest; / Kṛṣṇa takes delight in play there, surrounded by Śrīdāman and others.
The thirteenth petal is excellent; the forest Bhadra is remembered there. / The fourteenth petal is declared to be the place bestowing all supernatural perfections.
The delightful Śrīvana is there, the cause of all sovereign power, / consisting of petals of Kṛṣṇa's play, increasing beauty, splendor, and fame.
The fifteenth petal is excellent; the Lohavana is remembered there. / The sixteenth petal is described as equal in glorification to the pericarp.
Mahāvana is sung there; in it is the supreme mystery. / There he delights in childhood sports, surrounded by cowherd boys.
The slaying of Pūtanā and others is there, and the breaking of the twin Arjuna trees. / The presiding deity there is the child cowherd, five years of age,
proclaimed by the name Dāmodara, an ocean of the aesthetic joy of loving bliss. / This famous petal is spoken of as the best petal of all.
The filaments are Kṛṣṇa's play, spoken of as the petal of pastimes; / and the petal of filaments is declared to be chief among the perfected.
Pārvatī said: / What is the wondrous glorification or the secret of the forest of Vṛndā? / I wish to hear that; please tell me, O great lord!
The Lord said: / It is told to you, my dearest, as the secret beyond secrets, highest of the high, / that secret of secrets, and rarest of the rare,
hidden in the three worlds, O goddess, well-worshiped by the lord of the gods, / the place desired by Brahmā and the others, served by gods, Siddhas, and others.
Great lords of yoga, indeed, are always single-mindedly devoted to its contemplation with devotion; / and continuous dance and song are performed by Apsarases and Gandharvas.
Glorious Vṛndāvana is delightful, the refuge of the aesthetic joy of complete bliss, / its ground made of wishing-gems, its water nectar filled with aesthetic joy,
the tree there is the wishing-tree, attended by herds of wishing-cows; / every woman is Lakṣmī, every man is Viṣṇu, born of a tenth portion of him.
There his form is of youthful age, an eternal embodiment of bliss, / whose gait is dance, whose sweet talk is music, with an ever-smiling face,
resorted to by Vaiṣṇavas endowed with pure sattva and filled with love, / immersed in the bliss of the absolute Brahman, radiant, composed of his form, absorbed in him,
resounding sweetly and enchantingly with intoxicated cuckoos, bees, and the like, / with the singing of parrots on cheeks, and thousands of intoxicated bees,
abounding in the dancing of peacocks, with the charm of all fragrances, / and filled with the pollen of flowers of various colors.
where the full moon is in eternal rise, attended by the gentle rays of the sun, / free from sorrow, destroying pain, devoid of old age and death;
free from anger, gone beyond envy, undivided, free from egoism, / having the nectar-essence of full bliss, an ocean of the joy of full love;
the great abode beyond the qualities, whose very nature is full love, / where trees and other beings shed tears of loving bliss with hairs standing on end—
what then can be said of the devotees of Viṣṇu endowed with consciousness? / By the touch of the dust of Govinda's feet, Vṛndāvana is eternal upon the earth.
Vṛndāvana is the pericarp of the thousand-petalled lotus, / by mere touch of which the earth is blessed in the three worlds.
Secret of secrets, charming, Vṛndāvana is in the middle of the earth, / the imperishable, supreme bliss, the immutable abode of Govinda;
undivided from Govinda's body, the resting place of the happiness of the complete Brahman; / liberation comes from the touch of its dust—what can be said of its glory?
Therefore, O goddess, hold that forest in your heart with all your being, / and Kṛṣṇa, whose form is that of youth, sporting in Vṛndāvana.
And the Kālindī circumambulated its pericarp; / its water is profound with playful dissolution, enchanting with fragrance,
blended with the nectar of bliss, an abundant abode of floral nectar, / radiant with flowers of various colors such as lotuses and water lilies,
charming with its waters adorned by ruddy geese and other birds / with lovely, varied sweet calls, exceedingly delightful with its waves.
Its two delightful banks are made of pure gold; / it is declared to be ten million times greater than the Gaṅgā, where the pericarp is touched.
It is ten million times greater in the pericarp, where Hari is engaged in play; / Kṛṣṇa, the pericarp, and the Kālindī are undivided, a single form.
Pārvatī said: / What is the wonder of Govinda, whose form is fashioned of beauty? / That I wish to hear; tell me, O ocean of compassion.
The Lord said: / In the middle of charming Vṛndāvana, adorned with lovely anklets, / ornamented with the branches and sprouts of excellent trees extending for a yojana,
in its center, in a lovely mansion, is the radiant seat of yoga, / constructed with eight corners, captivating with various splendors.
Upon it is an auspicious lion-throne of ruby jewels; / on that is an eight-petalled lotus, an abode of bliss in its pericarp,
the supreme place of Govinda—how can its glory be described?— / attended by the multitude of cowherd women standing within the sacred mantra of Govinda.
One should meditate upon Kṛṣṇa, the sovereign of Vṛndāvana, having a divine form of the youth of Vraja, / the king of Vraja, possessing perpetual majesty, the sole beloved of the youths of Vraja;
whose youth is burgeoning from early youth, whose form is wondrous in age, / the beginning of all without a beginning, the beloved son of the cowherd Nanda;
sought by the Vedas, unborn, eternal, captivating the hearts of the cowherd women, / the supreme abode, the supreme form, two-armed, the lord of Gokula;
the delight of the cowherd maiden, the sole cause of the quality-less Brahman; / glorious, fresh, pure, captivating as a dark abode;
very glossy like a bank of fresh rain-clouds, with lovely earrings, / having the fine luster of a blossoming blue lotus, delightful to touch, bringing happiness;
smooth and charmingly dark, resembling a mass of crushed collyrium, / with very glossy, dark, curling locks of hair of endless fragrance;
above that, enchanting with a dark crest [tilted] to the right side, / brilliant with various colors, adorned with a gleaming peacock feather;
having a lovely crest of Mandāra flowers and a cow's tail, beautifully adorned; / sometimes adorned with a crown of rows of large feathers;
sometimes ornamented with a diadem of many gems and rubies; / surrounded by trembling curls, his face resembling ten million shining moons;
wearing a musk tilaka, shining, accompanied by charming yellow orpiment, / with eyes like very long petals of the extremely glossy blue lotus;
with a smile clinging to his dancing brow-creepers, with a sidelong glance, / exceedingly enchanting with the tip of his nose possessing very lovely, elevated beauty;
captivating the three worlds with the luster of the pearl from an elephant on the tip of his nose, / deeply charming with his lower lip very glossy and red as vermilion;
wearing makara-shaped earrings of gold flashing with various colors, / with cheeks reflecting their mass of rays, glistening like a mirror;
adorned with lotuses at his ears, fine Mandāra flowers, and makara ear-ornaments, / with the Śrīvatsa and the Kaustubha upon his chest, his throat gleaming with a pearl necklace;
with shining divine rubies blended with lovely gold, / with bracelets and armlets on his hands, and his hips adorned with a girdle of small bells;
resplendent with glorious feet possessing the beauty of lovely anklets; / with shining camphor, agallochum, musk, sandalwood, and the like;
variegated with divine ointments mixed with yellow orpiment and other pastes; / resplendent with glossy yellow silk, swinging down to the foreparts of his feet;
with a deep navel lotus, a line of hair bent like a garland, / with a pair of well-rounded knees, and charming lotus feet;
adorned on the soles of his feet and hands with the flag, thunderbolt, goad, and lotus, / the rows of beams from whose moon-like nails are the sole cause of the complete Brahman.
Some declare a part of him to be the non-dual Brahman whose form is consciousness; / the wise proclaim Mahāviṣṇu to be a tenth part of that.
That very form is meditated upon in the heart by the lords of yoga and by Sanaka and the others; / bent in three places, fashioned from the essence of all graceful creations;
with his neck turned sideways, more handsome than countless tens of millions of Kamas; / having his fine cheek placed on his left shoulder, wearing flashing golden earrings;
smiling with a glance from the corner of his eye, more handsome than ten million Kamas; / with the lovely, melodious sounds of the flute placed upon his curved lower lip,
enchanting the three worlds, immersed in the ocean of nectar of love. / Śrī Pārvatī said: The supreme cause, Kṛṣṇa, the great station named Govinda,
the eternal sovereign of Vṛndāvana, the sole cause of that which is beyond qualities— / what is that wondrous and beautiful secret glorification of his?
Speak of that, O God of gods! I wish to hear it, O Lord. / The Lord said: The limit of the glory of the moonbeam from his toenails is not reached;
how much of his glory can be told, O goddess? Listen with joy. / In the infinite millions of universes, in the endless expansion of the three qualities,
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara are fractional portions of ten million times ten million parts of his portions; / endowed with creation, maintenance, and the like, they remain as his splendors.
Portions that are fractions of ten million times ten million parts of his form, having the bodies of Kama, / cast delusion upon the world, abiding within those cosmic eggs.

Who is the all-pervading lord that is a fraction of ten million times ten million parts of the luster shining from his body? / The forms of the sun are but the rays of a ten-millionth part of his light.
By the rays of his own body, which are the nectar-essence of supreme bliss, / whose form is consciousness of supreme joy, the sole causes of that which is beyond qualities,
Rays of light, portions of a myriadth part of his parts, sustain life; / the splendours of the moon-like gems are the nails of his pair of lotus feet.
they call the cause even of the complete Brahman, difficult to attain by the Vedas. / An endless, ten-millionth part of the fragrance of his portion enchants the universe.
The origin of diverse fragrances such as flowers and scents comes from his touch. / His beloved, however, is the primordial material nature, Rādhikā, the beloved of Kṛṣṇa;
Durgā and the others, composed of the three qualities, are fractions of ten million times ten million parts of her portions. / From the touch of the dust of her feet, ten million Viṣṇus are born.

5.70.m:
Pārvatī said:
Its attendants, who are the attendants of the Lord—
that I wish to hear; tell me, O ocean of compassion!

The Lord said:
Govinda, seated on a golden throne with Rādhā,
having the previously described beauty and charm, with divine ornaments, garments, and garlands,

bent in three places, charming and very tender, the pupil of the cowherd maidens' eyes;
and outside that, on the yoga seat surrounded by a golden throne,

filled with intense longing in every limb, the principal beloveds of Kṛṣṇa,
Lalitā and others who are portions of Prakṛti, and the primordial Prakṛti, Rādhikā.

Goddess Lalitā is in front, Śyāmalā in the northwest corner,
Śrīmatī Dhanyā in the north, the beloved of Śrī Hari in the northeast,

and Viśākhā in the east, then Śaibyā in the southeast,
and Padmā in the south, and then in the southwest they stand in succession.

On the yoga seat, at the tip of the filaments, is the lovely beloved Candrāvatī;
they are the eight holy primary Prakṛtis, beloved of Kṛṣṇa.

The primary Prakṛti, however, is the first, Rādhā, equal to Candrāvatī,
Candrāvalī, Citrarekhā, Candrā, Madanasundarī,

and the beloved Śrī Madhumatī, Candrarekhā, and Haripriyā;
these sixteen are the primary Prakṛtis, beloved of Kṛṣṇa.

Rādhā, the queen of Vṛndāvana, and likewise the beloved Candrāvalī,
having undivided virtues, charm, and beauty, with lovely eyes,

charming, in innocent dress, radiant in adolescent youth;
and in front of them are other cowherd girls by the thousands,

shining like a mass of pure gold, very bright, with beautiful eyes,
with their hearts fixed on his form, eager for his embrace,

immersed in the nectar-essence of the Dark One, their minds manifesting his mood,
their consciousness offered to the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, which are worshipped with blue-lotus eyes.

Then on the right are the daughters of the Śrutis, accompanied by tens of thousands,
whose appearance enchants the world, with longing for Kṛṣṇa dwelling in their hearts,

who have enchanted the three worlds with various melodies of pure tones,
singing hidden secrets there, overwhelmed with love.

Then on the left are the daughters of the gods, in divine dress, radiant with aesthetic emotion,
skilled in various clever arts, endowed with an abundance of divine sentiments,

rich in extraordinary beauty, with side-glances most charming,
free from shame there towards Govinda, intent on touching his body,

their minds immersed in devotion to him, with smiling, oblique glances.
Then outside the temple, which was surrounded brightly by the beloved,

equal in dress and age, equal in strength and prowess,
equal in virtues and deeds, fond of equal ornaments,

intent on singing in unison and playing the flute,
Śrīdāman is at the western gate, likewise Vasudāman in the north,

and Sudāman in the east, and also Kiṅkiṇī in the south;
and outside that, on a golden seat surrounded by a golden temple,

standing within a golden altar, adorned with golden ornaments,
[surrounding] Stokakṛṣṇa, Subhadra, and others, with cowherd boys by tens of thousands,

with horns, vīṇās, flutes, and canes, with age, dress, appearance, and voices,
endowed with meditation on his qualities, singing and ecstatic.
Appearing as if portrayed in a painting, radiant with wonder, continually shedding tears of bliss, / their entire bodies overwhelmed with horripilation, like lordly yogins struck with amazement,
surrounded by countless Govindas immune to decay. / Outside that, within a golden rampart blazing like ten million suns,
there is a great garden in the four directions, intoxicating with charming fragrance. / In the western quarter, facing forward, at the base of a splendid pārijāta tree,
beneath it on a golden pedestal adorned with golden ornaments, / in its center on a radiant, heavenly throne studded with jewels and rubies,
upon it sits supreme bliss, Vāsudeva, Lord of the universe, / whose form is consciousness beyond the three guṇas, the cause of all causes,
dark like an indranīla gem or a dense cloud, with curling dark blue locks, / with broad eyes like lotus petals and earrings shaped like makaras,
four-armed, bearing the weapons of discus, sword, mace, conch, and lotus, / without beginning or end, eternal, the primary Puruṣottama,
whose form is light, the great abode, ancient, wearing a garland of forest flowers, / clad in yellow garments, lovely, adorned with celestial ornaments,
anointed with heavenly unguents, charming with limbs splendidly decorated. / There Rukmiṇī, Satyabhāmā, and Nāgnajitī of auspicious marks,
Mitravindā, Anuvindā, Sunandā, beloved Jāmbavatī, / and Suśīlā—these eight noble women, beloved of Vāsudeva—
shine forth, accompanied by attendants devoted to their service. / To the north, in a vast garden sheltered by haricandana trees,
there, beneath on a golden pedestal adorned with a jeweled pavilion, / in its center, on a throne radiant with golden petals,
resides Sankarṣaṇa with Revatī, bearing the plow as his weapon, / the Lord's beloved Ananta, non-different in qualities and form,
resembling pure crystal, with eyes like red lotus petals, / wearing blue silk, tender, adorned with celestial ornaments, garlands, and garments,
ever devoted to drinking sweet wine, his eyes rolling with intoxication. / To the south, in an inner chamber located within the center,
at the foot of a santāna tree adorned with a jeweled temple, / in its center, upon a radiant heavenly throne of jewels and rubies,
the god Pradyumna dwells comfortably above it with Rati, / the embodiment of the aesthetic essence of the highest beauty captivating the universe,
shining like a mass of dark blue lotuses, with eyes like lotus petals, / adorned with celestial ornaments and coated with divine fragrant ointments,
his astonishing form possessing all the beauty that enchants the universe. / In the eastern garden, a great grove sheltered by wish-granting trees,
there, beneath on a golden pedestal adorned with a golden pavilion, / in its center, on an established, radiant, and heavenly throne,
the glorious Aniruddha, Lord of the universe, sits together with the divine Uṣā, / dense with bliss, dark as a cloud, very sleek, with curling black locks,
with beautiful, arched eyebrows curved like creepers, handsome cheeks, and a fine nose, / a graceful neck, and an exceedingly captivating, handsome chest,
wearing a diadem and earrings, adorned with throat ornaments, / having an exceedingly beautiful form charming with delicate anklets,
worshiped by a host of beloved servants, fond of music where [it is sung], / the complete Brahman, eternal bliss, whose intrinsic nature is pure sattva.
Above him in the intermediate space sits Viṣṇu, Lord of all lords, / beginningless, the primeval consciousness, bliss of consciousness, supreme, all-pervading,
beyond the three guṇas, unmanifest, eternal, imperishable, immutable, / with a dark body possessing the beauty and sweetness of a mass of clouds,
exceedingly beautiful with sleek, dark blue curly locks, / with long, charming, glossy eyes resembling lotus petals,

with a diadem and earrings illuminating his cheeks, surrounded by those whose essence is pure sattva, / and by those delighted in the Self, who are consciousness itself, absorbed in meditation on his form;
with that meditation mounted in their hearts and their gaze fixed on the tip of their nose, / causeless devotion is performed by them through the expressions of body and heart.
To his left, by Yakṣas, Gandharvas, Siddhas, Vidyādharas, and others, / along with lovely hosts of Apsarases devoted to dance and song,
yearning intensely to worship his body, eager for Kṛṣṇa; / and before him in the sky on comfortable seats, by all the Vaiṣṇavas,
by Prahlāda, Nārada, and others, by Kumāra, Śuka, and the Vaiṣṇavas, / by Janaka and others, with radiant devotion, devoted to inner and outer manifestations;
all their limbs bristling with horripilation, overwhelmed with surging love, / sprinkled with the nectar of mystery, [they chant] the four-syllable mantra.
This crest-jewel of mantras is proclaimed as the sole source of all mantras; / among all mantras of the divine, youth is the source of mantras;
the crest-jewel mantra is the origin of all youth-mantras. / Those who have taken shelter in the joy of complete love recite it mentally;
they desire unswerving devotion of love at his lotus feet. / Outside that, within a very high, delightful enclosure made of crystal and other stones,
scattered on all four sides with white and red saffron and other powders, / sits a white, four-armed Viṣṇu as the western gatekeeper,
adorned with conch, discus, mace, lotus, diadem, and other ornaments. / A red, four-armed one wielding lotus, conch, discus, and mace,
radiant with diadem and earrings, stands as gatekeeper in the north. / A fair-complexioned, four-armed Viṣṇu wielding conch, discus, and mace,
adorned with diadem, earrings, and the like, wearing a forest garland, / is proclaimed as the fair gatekeeper at the eastern gate.
Black-complexioned, four-armed, adorned with conch, discus, and other attributes, / the gatekeeper of the south is glorious Viṣṇu, black in color.
Whoever, pure and restrained, reads this deed of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, / or hears it with devotion, attains delight in Govinda.
